No. The browser has no idea; it treats whatever comes back for an img src as an image and reads the bytes.
While rendering HTML it reaches the tag and sends an HTTP GET to the src URL; it expects an image and treats what comes back as one.

On a successful response it reads the first bytes (format signature, e.g. PNG 89 50 4E 47, JPEG FF D8 FF), picks the matching decoder and paints pixels. SVG is the exception: recognised by Content-Type image/svg+xml.

The server finds the handler that owns /static; whatever follows /static is treated as a relative file path in the mapped folder (img/arpit.jpg); the handler reads that file and sends its bytes, regardless of type.

is_active in photos: join on reads, two updates in a transaction plus locks and ownership check, 'two active' / 'none active' states possible. active_photo_id: read is one row by hash, no join; mark active is one UPDATE of one column, those bad states can't happen, concurrent requests leave the last choice; slightly faster but mainly simpler.

Hit: CDN answers from cache. Miss: CDN calls the API, which asks the DB which photo is active, reads bytes from S3, returns through the CDN, which caches it 1-2 days.

API writes DB/S3, puts a photo_updated event on Kafka; an invalidation worker calls the CDN's purge API for the path (and all widths); next request misses and fetches the new photo. (Or call purge synchronously.)
Users expect the new photo everywhere now; with a 1-2 day TTL others could see the old face for up to two days. Long TTL for speed, explicit purge for correctness.

{src, dest, msg}: who sent what to whom. Workers SADD dest src, i.e. sender added to recipient's Redis set.

The clear must also delete B's keys in the aux store, so it must know which keys are B's (read them off B's set, or use one hash per user: HSETNX/DEL B).

It isn't money: worst case the badge shows 2 not 3 until next tap; the glitch isn't fatal, while the whole messaging system going down would be. Trade a little inconsistency for throughput; TTL heals drift.
Stop counting past a point (e.g. show 100+): once the set is past the threshold, skip writes even for new senders (but needs knowing the size).
Aux: one existence key per pair, e.g. B_C (or a hash B with field C). Main: key B with a set of senders {C, D}.
Aux write succeeds, main fails: C recorded as seen but never added; badge undercounts (e.g. 2 while 300 messages wait) until next tap clears both.
